sources.cite: J. C. Lagarias, The set of rational cycles for the 3x+1 problem, Acta Arith. 56 (1990) 33-53, Thm 2.1 and Sect. 1
sources.what: every 0-1 parity vector v of length L gives a unique rational cycle x(v) = N(v)/(2^L - 3^{|v|}); rational cycles correspond one-to-one to primitive cycles of T_k (k = denominator). Taking an irreducible v with n ones and 2^L > 3^n (resp. < 3^n, then negate) gives the required positive primitive cycle of 3x+k (resp. 3x-k); this corollary is not stated explicitly

prior_art.note: Existence (3x+k, n odd elements) is an immediate corollary of Lagarias 1990 Thm 2.1 plus the rational-cycle/primitive-cycle correspondence, but no source states it for these entries; our explicit cycles via 3^n - 2^n are a concrete instance.
